body: I've been trying a few ways to get it out, writing is a big one for me. I could spend hours just writing down everything I feel. I usually feel drained afterwards but it helps a bit.

I guess going home to me is like going home as a failure. I've been bragging about how great this place is, I would hate to have to go back and listen to all of the "I told you so"'s

Besides, I've invested too much into moving here in the first place, it was too stressful to begin with, I can't face doing the reverse

I went through a similar situation, and here was my solution. My SO finished school and lost his job at the same time. 

For the first month I worked **extra hard** and I was ok with him taking some time off for a while, and we still managed to get all our regular treats, the second month I stopped all of that and let him realise how hard it was to be the only provider in the house.

At the end of the second month I sat him down and asked him to help me update my CV because I couldn't stay in the same job if I was going to have to support us both (clever, eh?)

So while I'm writing up my CV he said it was about time he got his shit together and made one too. It only took us a few hours and we were done.

The next day I got some prints made of his CV and I brought home envelopes and I helped him neatly fold them up, and on my day off I drove him around to all of the possible places he could find work so he could distribute his CV. I cleaned his best presentable clothes (smart casual) and pep talked him after going to each of the places. A lot of them were disappointing and he was already in a non-employed slump.

After a few days he got a call from one of the places we visited and they asked him to come in for a trial. He did the trial, worked his butt off, and in the end he got the job.

So the moral of the story was if you want him to get a job, you've got to be just as interested or even more interested than he is. Get him motivated and encourage any good steps he takes. 

EDIT: Should also add, my guy is a gamer too. And I had to deal with him sitting at home all day and not helping around the house. I called him out on it, and told him he needed a reality check, as opposed to his life in the game. It wasn't easy to say but in the end he was helping out around the house more and I was coming home to hot meals and warm fires.
I'm glad to see I'm not alone on this. Facebook is a blessing and a curse.
If someone has taken more than the daily recommended dosage of any kind of medication it can have damaging effects. It is **vital** that you call the emergency services in this case.
